setting.note: Conrad invents a whole South American republic, Costaguana, and its silver port Sulaco, then fills it with revolutions and a hoard of mine silver that corrupts everyone it touches; the fictional coast is built from the real northern shore of South America Conrad had seen, anchored here to Colombia's Caribbean rim.

rights.originalWork: First published in 1904 by Joseph Conrad; long out of copyright. Mapped as a cited work: no text stored, no passages reproduced. The places are facts and the notes are our own.
rights.textSource: None stored. A cited book reproduces no text.
rights.territoryNotes: Locations and original commentary only. No reproduction of any text, in any territory.
rights.attribution: Nostromo, Joseph Conrad (1904). Locations mapped by Read the Places; Costaguana and Sulaco are fictional, anchored to the real northern-South-American coast.

palette.note: The dull gleam of the San Tomé silver that drives and poisons the story. A cited book's colour is not a quotation; it still has to be legible, and this clears WCAG AA on paper.
